quotes.text: Let the unity of Christians be our polar star.
With you all we desire to unite in the bonds of an entire Christian unity
The Church of Christ upon earth is essentially, intentionally, and constitutionally one
We will, that this body die, be dissolved, and sink into union with the Body of Christ at large

Should any one think it lawful to paganize both the Greek and Latin churches—to eject one hundred millions of members of the Greek and Roman communions from the visible and invisible precincts of the Christian family
and regard the Protestant faith and people as the only true faith and the only true citizens of the kingdom of Jesus; what then shall we say of them

Of forty millions of Protestants shall we constitute the visible kingdom of the Prince of Peace? Be it so, for the sake of argument; and what then? The Christian army is forty millions strong; but how do they muster? Under forty ensigns? Under forty antagonist leaders? Would to God there were but forty!
if there be no Christians in the Protestant sects, there are certainly none among the Romanists
and therefore no Christians in the world except ourselves

Therefore, for many centuries there has been no church of Christ, no Christians in the world; and the promises concerning the everlasting kingdom of Messiah have failed, and the gates of hell have prevailed against his church! This cannot be; and therefore there are Christians among the sects.
I circumscribe not the Divine philanthropy—the Divine grace. I dare not say that there is no salvation in the church of Rome, or in that of Constantinople
nor, indeed, is there anything either in Scripture or the nature of things that should induce us to expect an entire unity of sentiment in the present imperfect state.

for no man can relinquish his opinions or practices till once convinced that they are wrong; and this he may not be immediately, even supposing they were so. One thing, however, he may do: when not bound by an express command, he need not impose them upon others
we charitably hope that, in due time, God will reveal even this unto them; only let such neither refuse to come to the light, nor yet, through prejudice, reject it when it shines upon them.
The Church may, and we believe will, come to such a Scriptural unity of faith and practice, that there will be no schism in the body
a still higher and more perfect degree of uniformity is intended, though neither in the first nor second instance, which are but so many steps toward it
If you think your brother in error, labor in the spirit of love and meekness to convince him; but imposing zeal against him will only harden him
A little longer forbearance with each others weakness, and truth will triumph.
An Address to the Churches of Christ,

It is urged by many churches that one part of worship every Lord’s day, is to break bread, others are not so well convinced of this as being a duty. It is humbly hoped that mutual forbearance will be exercised, one towards the other on this practice, till we all come into the unity of the faith.
